findings.evidence: Lines 88–90, 142–144, and 191–193 declare equivalences between `G.fullyBlockedHomology` types; `rg` confirms there is no `fullyBlockedCycleSubquotient` declaration, while adjacent `Homology/Basic.lean:120` uses `fullyBlockedHomologyEquivChainOfLeTwo`.
findings.fix: Rename the three definitions and their six `_mk`/`_symm_mk` lemmas to `fullyBlockedHomology{Transpose,Rotate,SwapMarkings}Equiv...` (or rename the underlying type consistently if it is intentionally not called homology).
findings.issue: All three `fullyBlockedCycleSubquotient{Transpose,Rotate,SwapMarkings}Equiv` families name neither their source/target declaration nor adjacent API terminology; their types are `fullyBlockedHomology`, and the naming convention says definition names should appear in theorem names when unambiguous.

summary: The new equivalence family is named after a nonexistent “cycle subquotient” API instead of the established `fullyBlockedHomology` type, making the declarations difficult to discover consistently.
